item.content:encoded:
Aw, the poor thing, being confused and trapped in an unfamiliar body all the time!

The only part that's weird to me (I know, right?) is that it's carnivorous. Seeing as it's constantly being assembled from all sorts of different types of pieces, it just seems to me that it would be an omnivore. Not that every single thing has to make sense, but I thought I would throw it out there anyway.

It makes me a little sad when people are quick to make comments like, "yeah, whatever, we already have one," in a dismissive way. Just because something similar already exists (which is bound to happen here and there with so many entries) doesn't mean we can't have both. Use that similar entry to make sure the new one is unique! People should be encouraged to write more, to come at things from a different perspective, to take their idea to a different place.

I get it, telling someone their idea already exists on the site is a way of letting them know they should do something different, and a comment that amounts to "it's been done. NEXT," might possibly be on the constructive side of criticism, but it mostly just sounds like trying to shut them down. We're adults, we can handle criticism, but there needs to be some actual criticism to handle, you know?

Well, now that I've said all that in a place where it will be seen by like, 6 people ever (two of whom are actually the same person who had simply forgotten that they had already read these comments before), I'M OUT!

item.content:encoded: I really like the concept, but the way it's described consistently brings to mind describing one's pet to a friend. For example, "flat face". Is it two dimensional? Is it like that of a pug? (If it is intentionally ambiguous, please disregard) Also, "patches" are introduced out of nowhere. How does the Foundation identify/designate a "patch"? Is it an arbitrary section of connected tissues from the same animal? Is it a measured/numbered section of SCP-422? The phrases "weeks ago" and "minutes ago" break the clinical tone for me. Otherwise, it's pretty well executed, and the idea of it some day saying "Da…ddy" makes me shiver. Neutral vote.
